thief-t02-02.model_answer: Hari Singh's decision to return the stolen money becomes a turning point because it shows that he is beginning to value honesty and education. He realises that Anil's trust is more important than the money he has taken. He also understands that Anil can teach him to read, write and build a better future. The possibility of losing this opportunity makes him reconsider his actions. Returning the money is therefore not merely an act of regret but the beginning of a change in character. Hari starts moving away from a life of theft and towards an honest life. Anil's trust gives him a reason to choose that better path.

thief-t03-02.model_answer: Trust becomes more powerful than punishment in Hari Singh's transformation because Anil treats him with confidence and kindness. Anil gives Hari food, shelter and an opportunity to learn instead of constantly suspecting him. When Hari steals the money, he realises that losing Anil's trust would also mean losing the chance for education. The money is temporary, while the knowledge and future Anil can offer are more valuable. Hari therefore decides to return the money even though he could have escaped with it. His conscience is strengthened by the trust Anil has placed in him. The story suggests that understanding and faith in a person's ability to change can sometimes achieve more than punishment.

tiger-t03-02.model_answer: The poem contrasts the tiger's imagined life in the jungle with his actual life in the zoo. In the jungle he would move through grass, hunt prey and live according to his natural instincts. He would have freedom to choose where to go and how to survive. In the zoo he is trapped behind bars and can only pace within a small space. He cannot hunt or experience the open forest. His quiet anger and repeated movement show his frustration. The contrast makes captivity appear unnatural and encourages the reader to sympathise with the tiger.

trees-t03-02.model_answer: The struggle of the trees suggests a strong desire for freedom and a return to the natural world. The trees are personified as though they are living beings trapped inside a house. Their roots work free and their branches strain towards the forest outside. This struggle shows that nature resists artificial confinement. The movement also symbolises the human desire to escape restrictions and regain independence. The poet presents freedom as something natural and deeply necessary. Thus the trees' struggle becomes a wider image of liberation.

triumph-t02-02.model_answer: Tricki recovers without medicine because his real problem is caused by overfeeding and lack of exercise. At home Mrs Pumphrey gives him rich food and treats because she mistakes pampering for proper care. At the surgery, Herriot puts him on a controlled diet. Tricki also becomes active by playing and exercising with the other dogs. His body gradually becomes healthier and his energy returns. No special medicine is needed because a sensible routine addresses the actual cause of his illness. The story shows that moderation and discipline are often more effective than unnecessary treatment.

triumph-t03-02.model_answer: Tricki's recovery shows that discipline and sensible care can be more useful than excessive pampering. At home Mrs Pumphrey overfed him and gave him too many rich treats while providing little exercise. As a result, Tricki became fat, lazy and unhealthy. At the surgery he received a controlled diet and regular exercise with other dogs. He gradually became active and fit without needing special medicines. The experience shows that affection should not become overindulgence. Proper food, exercise and a balanced routine are essential for good health.

trust-t03-02.model_answer: Horace's belief that he is a careful thief is ironic because his confidence in his own cleverness leads directly to his downfall. He plans his burglaries carefully and believes he takes sensible precautions. However, another thief deceives him by pretending to be the owner of the house. Horace accepts the false story and opens the safe for her. He also removes his gloves, leaving fingerprints that can identify him. The person who thinks he is an expert criminal is therefore tricked by someone more clever. The irony is completed when Horace is arrested while the real thief escapes.

wild-t03-02.model_answer: Rhyme plays an important role in making 'How to Tell Wild Animals' lively and humorous. The regular rhyming pattern gives the poem a playful rhythm. It makes the unusual descriptions of dangerous animals easier to remember. Rhyme also supports the comic tone because serious dangers are presented in a light, entertaining manner. Together with exaggeration and irony, it turns the poem into a humorous set of identification clues. The playful combination of these devices keeps the poem entertaining while making its descriptions easy to remember.
